_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — VERBATIM EXTRACTION FOR SENIOR FOUR PHYSICAL EDUCATION

values: Honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

themes.theme_title: Theory and Practice of Physical Education

topic_metadata.topic_title: HEALTH, PHYSICAL ACTIVITY AND STRESS MANAGEMENT

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the importance of physical exercises in maintaining a stress free and healthy body and mind.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: illustrate the different ways that they can keep healthy including by performing physical exercises to improve personal fitness. (u, s)
perform physical exercises to manage stress and emotions. (s,a)
understand the different applications of different fitness components in daily life.(u)
engage in fitness exercises for lifelong well-being. (s,v,a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Guide the learners to take each of the well-being terms mentioned below and explain in more detail what they think they mean; - physical wellbeing - mental wellbeing - social wellbeing - fitness and health
Each learner designs an individual plan on how to keep active and health and indicates how to practice the activities in their plan.
In groups, learners do a research on lifestyles that cause emotional stress, write a report and share their findings.
In groups, learners discuss and generate ideas why stress management helps one to keep healthy.
Learners are guided to practice physical activities that can help one to relax and manage stress.
Learners use physical rehearsals as a way of releasing tension.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Task learners to develop a training session with activities that they think can be used by a student to manage stress/ emotions. And in a write-up explain how the suggested activities contribute to stress management.
Observe the learners’ performance noting: generic skills of creativity, team work, leadership, respect; appropriateness of activities chosen.

In a conversation: ascertain the impact of learners’ input in relation to the final output as they perform the skill; ask learners to describe the measures put in place to ensure a safe environment for play.
Proper execution lifesaving skills

topics.core_competency: The learner performs intermediate aerobics skills, and applies these skills in designing and conducting sessions for healthy living.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: perform basic aerobics movements with higher level of mastery during aerobics sessions. (s)
perform intermediate aerobic steps and arm movements in aerobics. (s)
display the advanced movement skills in aerobics sessions while exhibiting strength, flexibility and endurance. (s,u)
plan and conduct aerobics sessions. (s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners are given turns to run aerobics session using basic aerobics moves.

Learners observe and practice the following intermediate steps of aerobics individually and in small groups; 8 & 16 count steps: I-step, K-step, L-step, Repeater, Rocking Horse, Split Basic, Straddle, T-step, X-step, Y-step, Z-step.

Learners are guided to practice the following arm movements in aerobics individually and in small groups; arm movements: low row, overhead press, overhead pull, pec press, slice, shoulder punch, triceps kickbacks, up-right row.
As a class, learners are guided on the components of an aerobics session.
In small groups, learners draft a plan to conduct aerobics. They should critically evaluate the quality of each other’s aerobics sessions.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to 1. illustrate intermediate movement skills on rhythm. 2. exhibit the physical fitness qualities of strength, flexibility, ability and endurance while performing advanced aerobics. 3. display aesthetic quality, positive attitude towards participation in advanced aerobics. 4. design a plan for aerobics and execute it.
Observe the learners’ performance and keep a record of their progression.
Probe learners in a conversation to ascertain their understanding of the relevance of the different movements.

topics.core_competency: The learner performs various swimming strokes and observes safety measure while in water.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: apply the basic water movements while in water. (s)
perform basic swimming strokes. (s)
observe safety while in water. (s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners are taken through and given time to practice the basic arm and leg movements in Front crawl.
In manageable groups, learners are taken through drills of breathing while swimming the Front crawl.
Learners are taken through and given time to practice the basic arm and leg movements in Breast stroke.
In manageable groups, learners are taken through drills of breathing while swimming the Breast stroke.
Learners are taken through and given time to practice the basic arm and leg movements in Back stroke.
In manageable groups, learners are taken through drills of body alignment, arm and leg actions in Back stroke.
Learners should be given the opportunity to watch others swim in order to learn from the swimming styles and strengths of others.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Ask learners to 1. illustrate the basic arm and leg movement in Front crawl and Breast stroke 2. display breathing in swimming the Front crawl and Breast strokes. 3. demonstrate different types of dives. 4. execute the Breast swimming stroke.
Observe the learners’ performance and keep a record of their progression.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies throwing skills and techniques to perform the throwing events in athletics as well as in other physical activities in daily life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: set up the throwing area for throws using improvised material. (s, gs,s,v,a)
apply rules for the throws through officiating. (s, v)
perform intermediate skills in javelin. (s)
perform intermediate skills in hammer. (s)
officiate the throws using the basic rules and regulations, developing intermediate skills across all ball games. (s)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners use previous knowledge to make throwing materials and to set up the areas for performing throws
Learners are guided through the rules that govern throws.
Learners listen, observe and then practice activities involving manipulation of missile, strength in arms and legs, coordination, gliding, hip twist (torque), recovery, etc.
Learners are guided to throw in the circle emphasizing proper hold and placement of missile in the groove of the neck and gliding.
Learners listen, observe and practice activities involving manipulation of missile, turning, co-ordination, hip torque, recovery, side on throw etc.
Learners put the shot using the O’Brien technique and throw the discus using one turn.
Learners are guided to practice and demonstrate the 5-step whole sequence throws in javelin throw.
Learners are guided to practice and demonstrate the Heel-toe turn (one turn) with 2-3 swings in hammer throw.
Learners interpret and apply the rules during throwing events.
Learners are assigned roles to officiate any throwing events.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Learners can 1. illustrate the 5-step rhythm in Javelin throw. 2. illustrate the single turn rotational technique in Discus throw. 3. demonstrate the heal-toe turn in hammer throw. 4. outline the regulations followed while officiating any throwing event of your choice.
Observe the learners’ performance and keep a record of their progression.
Probe learners in a conversation to ascertain their understanding of the relevance of the different movements.

themes.theme_title: Theory and practice of Physical Education

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the relevance of improved and equal access to sports.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the availability and access of different sports to the various groups of people in the community. (u)
advocate for the right to sports and play for all. (s,v,a)
develop ways of ensuring growth in facilities with access for participants/ performers with disabilities as well as women. (s,gs)
promote the relevance of sports in improving status of women in recent years. (gs, u,s,a)
design simple sports sessions to engage community. (s, gs)
engage in Community awareness creation on the importance of an active lifestyle.(gs,v,a)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In small groups, learners make a survey and document the available sports activities for different people in the community: special needs, children, youths, adults, and the old.
Learners, in a guided discovery, recognize the notion that sport should be accessible to all, irrespective of race, colour, gender, religious beliefs or disability.

In a class discussion, learners address the different pointers to discrimination such as access to sports equipment and play areas, access to the sports teachers and coaches, access to sportswear, frequency of sports trips and competitions.
As a class, learners identify some women sports personalities and discuss how sports has impacted on their status.

In groups, each designs a set of activities to form an inclusive sports session for their community. After the sessions, learners can suggest ways in which sports can contribute to the development of their community.
In small groups, learners produce articles for the school magazine or notice board highlighting the importance of an active lifestyle for all.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Task learners to 1. present a write-up of the status of sports access to different groups of people in their community. 2. justify the need for sports for all people in the community. 3. give ways in which a named discriminatory pointer can be addressed to enable access to sports for all. 4. explain ways in sports can improve the status of women. 5. state ways in which sports contributes to community development.
Observe the participation of learners and the use of generic skills.
Probe with conversations to ascertain their understanding.
Products should be write-ups, presentations, articles or posters where applicable.

topic_metadata.topic_title: PHYSICAL EDUCATION AND SPORTS FOR PEACE AND DEVELOPMENT

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the role of PE and sport in promoting Peace and Development.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the meaning of the peace and development. (u)
analyse the various ways that PES can be used to promote Development. (u, gs)
Understand the core values of sportsmanship that make sport a valuable method for promoting peace. (u, gs)
engage in physical activities that can be used to promote peace. (s, gs,)
design activities that can be used to promote peace. (gs, s)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners brainstorm and come up with the meaning of peace and development.
Learners in pairs identify the different ways that PES has promoted development in Uganda.
In their groups, learners are guided through discussion to propose other ways that PES can be used to promote Development.
Learners refer to previous lesson on agreeable behavior and identify the core values of sportsmanship that make sport a valuable method for promoting peace.
Learners are guided through activities that can be used to promote Peace.
In groups learners design activities that can be used to promote Peace in various categories of vulnerability such as Refugees, Ghetto/slum areas.
With reference to their communities learners in their groups design activities that can promote peace.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Task the learners to design activities that can be used to promote Peace among youth in Refugee camps.
Observe the learners’ performance noting: generic skills of creativity, team work, leadership, respect; appropriateness of activities chosen.
Engage learners in conversation to ascertain their understanding.
Keep a record of the learner’s performance.

topics.core_competency: The learner performs aerobics sessions using steps and moves from traditional dances and manages an aerobics session.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: perform a complete aerobics session. (s, gs,)
integrate traditional dance steps and moves into Aerobics and fitness sessions. (s, gs, u)
manage aerobics demonstrations at school level in a safe environment. (gs,s)
design unique aerobics sessions for fitness training. (s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners take turns to demonstrate and lead an aerobics session.
In small groups, learners make a selection of steps and moves from Ugandan traditional dances and match them to form an Aerobics session.
Learners in their groups can then practice the traditional move aerobic sessions that they formed.
In groups, learners make an integration of traditional dance moves into the classical ones forming full sessions at different levels and intensities.
In groups, learners are given tasks to execute in regard to the management of the displays: set up of the activity area, sound system, selection of music, management of the stage.
Different groups form teams, and organize competitive displays while other learners take roles in officiating the displays.
Learners take on a project to design an aerobics session for fitness building of their choice.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Task the learners to 1. run an aerobics session using selected traditional moves and steps. 2. create a mixed aerobics session using both traditional and classical steps. 3. explain the rules and regulations governing displays.
Observe the learners’ performance noting: generic skills of creativity, team work, leadership, respect; rhythmic floor of the movements.
Engage learners in conversation to ascertain their understanding
Keep a record of the learner’s performance

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: Learners take on a project to design an aerobics session for fitness building of their choice.

topics.core_competency: The learner performs the life saving techniques and applies these techniques while observing their own safety in water.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: perform the basic skills involved in life saving in a water environment. (s)
apply the skill of life saving as a rescue technique to ensure water safety. (s,u)
demonstrate how to identify a case that requires lifesaving skill for rescue. (u, s, gs)
apply knowledge and skills of water survival and rescue tactics. (s, gs,)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Learners then observe and practice basics of lifesaving using different objects such as life rings.
Learners observe and practice the life-saving strokes and techniques of back stroke and side stroke.
In a discussion, learners are guided to brainstorm on the meaning of life saving and the relevance of learning life saving techniques in water.
In groups, learners are guided through a discussion on the various lifesaving skills that can be used to ensure water safety.
Learner are guided to identify cases in water that require life saving for rescue.
In small groups, the learners are guided through and given time to practice survival swimming techniques namely; survival float, relaxation, water treading, swimming and undressing in water.

Learners are engaged in drills to practice dives for dodging and in pairs, they work together and practice deep water bobs and rehearse the lifesaving skills using any stroke and technique of their choice.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe: demonstration of the lifesaving skills by the learner; application of safety precautions; generic skills exhibited by learners.

In a conversation: ascertain the impact of learners’ input in relation to the final output as they perform the skill; ask learners to describe the measures put in place to ensure a safe environment for play.
Proper execution lifesaving skills.

topics.core_competency: The learner displays understanding and skills acquired form the practical activities in Athletics, Aesthetics and Games.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: demonstrate his/her understanding, knowledge and skills acquired in running, jumping and throwing events
Demonstrate his/her understanding, knowledge and skills in the activity chosen from Aesthetics
Demonstrate his/her understanding, knowledge and skills in the two activities chosen from Games

suggested_learning_activities.description: 1. Learner demonstrates skills of running, jumping and throwing 2. Leaner identifies the tools and equipment used for running, jumping and throwing events 3. Learner describes the rules and regulations followed in the running jumping and throwing events 4. Learner explains the safety precautions that should be considered for running jumping and throwing events

1. Learner illustrates the skills in the chosen activity 2. Learner describes the activity chosen from Aesthetics 3. Leaner mentions the rules and safety precautions followed while playing the chosen activity 4. Leaner explains the relevancy of the chosen activity to their daily life

1. Learner illustrates the skills in the chosen activities 2. Learner demonstrates the intermediate skills used in the chosen activities 3. Learner describes the activities chosen from Games 4. Leaner outlines the rules and safety precautions followed while playing the chosen activities 5. Leaner explains the relevancy of the chosen activities to their daily life

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe and keep a record each learners’ performance
Oral responses of the learners should be graded and a record of their performance made
The products of the learners performances should be recorded in a video for further reference
